9.text: While I was on St. Lawrence Island, I witnessed a performance by the

10.text: same shaman. His name was Assuˊnaṛak, and he belonged to a family

11.text: renowned for shamanistic skill through several generations. Among other

12.text: tricks, he made me throw a skin coverlet over his bare shoulders while he

13.text: kept his arms tightly crossed over his breast. This was done by the full

14.text: light of the lamp. The coverlet immediately stuck fast to his back, while I

15.text: held it by the free ends. The shaman was able, notwithstanding my resistance,

16.text: to haul me into the outer room of the house. He said, however, that he

17.text: was no longer able to sink into the ground, because, according to his words,

18.text: “this is not a time for great shamanistic acts.”

20.text: among shamans, but all the performances I witnessed were rather clumsy,

29.text: I have gone at length into the preceding details in order to show that

30.text: the shamanism of the Chukchee and the Asiatic Eskimo, though still in a

31.text: primitive stage of development, comprises, nevertheless, a number of complicated

32.text: tricks performed with the help of assistants. All of these have developed

36.text: SEXUAL PERVERSION AND TRANSFORMED SHAMANS. — A separate branch of

37.text: Chukchee shamanism, dealing with the perversion of sexual sense, has acquired

38.text: a somewhat peculiar form. The sexual organs play a part in various branches

39.text: of Chukchee shamanism. Especially do the malignant spells acquire additional

40.text: force through the performing of certain prescriptions regarding the organs of

41.text: sex, male and female. Thus, a “mischievous shaman,” when he desires to
